Transcripts summarized by tool counts, read set and final pointer only; no thought or usage events are reproduced.

parserOptionsRuling.question: Is ParserOptions.supportsComments (an already schema-owned computed getter) redundant eligible derived state that qualifies with comment under E3? Or is it an ineligible callable/schema-owned API? Does the stable D1 pair remain?
parserOptionsRuling.completeOwner: ParserOptions (ParserOptions.schema.ts:137-209) has 8 stored Boolean fields (:139,:141,:154,:155,:156,:161,:162,:163) plus 2 Boolean-valued get accessors (:198,:202), 10 in total. The >=2-Boolean recall precondition for the complete owner is met, so recall does not exclude any minimal cluster. comment (:150) is Option<string>; maxRows (:166) is NonNegativeInt; headers (:157) is Option<boolean|HeaderArray|fn>. None of the three is an extra Boolean member.
parserOptionsRuling.eligibility: Eligible for the net, but only as computed derived values. The getters are accessor properties of the ParserOptions instance type, read as options.supportsComments. They are not callables invoked by readers, not S.is schema guards, and not command/runtime handles. The atom rule says a Boolean counts by the value it owns or computes, and each getter computes exactly one Boolean. They are not stored state: they are absent from ParserOptions.fields and ParserOptions.Encoded, no constructor or decoder accepts them, and no writer exists.
parserOptionsRuling.e3Minimal: Not qualified. E3 targets a Boolean that duplicates a sibling payload's presence while being able to disagree with it, as in {isError, error?}. supportsComments is defined as O.isSome(this.comment) at :199. The joint (supportsComments, comment-presence) domain therefore has exactly 2 representable states, and both are legal. DECISIONS #1 requires a cardinality gap plus cited evidence, and there is no gap: the representable domain already equals the legal one. The design-law rider for derived instances (derive one value, or keep the source type in the view) is already satisfied, because the getter is a pure projection of the source. Guard-deletion accounting would be empty: no coherence check, if-chain or normalizer relates the two. The only readers are two test assertions, and the production parser reads comment directly (CsvParser.parser.ts:368). A design here would delete nothing, which the rider marks as misqualification.
parserOptionsRuling.limitRows: limitRows = Num.isGreaterThan(0)(maxRows) at :203. No binary axis or contract restriction is invented for maxRows. Csv.schema.ts:234 re-derives maxRows > 0 from the codec instead of reading the getter. That is duplication of a non-Boolean predicate, not Boolean creep.
parserOptionsRuling.pairD1: D1 stands. supportsComments and limitRows project two distinct, independently configured upstream fields (comment, maxRows). Fixtures cover (false,false) at test :22/:32 and (true,true) at :52/:55. (true,false) and (false,true) follow from setting only comment or only maxRows, and no guard excludes them.
parserOptionsRuling.result: Keep the stable r24-foundation-schema-n-z-parser-options-derived-gates D1 record unchanged: no cluster expansion, no qualification, no new record. Optional hygiene outside this campaign: both getters have zero production consumers, so a crispen pass could remove them. That is API-surface cleanup, not a boolean-creep finding. The `class-fields` kind is the closest available enum value for accessor members; no correction is proposed.
